title: Fallback tiering sandbox notes
content:
Context:
Quick personal sandbox for an idea I've been noodling: make fallback behavior (model/precision/region) a first-class, tiered policy attached to routes and customer budgets. Want something lightweight we can prototype in Hosted first, then move ideas to Dedicated/Private later.

Problem statement (short):
- Customers want predictable unit economics and stable latency. When primary model is expensive or temporarily overloaded, apps either time out or shoot up cost. Current runtime falls back in ad hoc ways (model variants or region routing) but lacks per-route policy definition and local simulation tools.

Goals for prototype:
- Define a simple tier model (T0/T1/T2) where T0=preferred (best quality, higher cost), T1=middling (quantized, lower-cost variant), T2=cheap/short (trimmed context or cached template)
- Allow route-level policy: e.g., marketing-chat -> keep T0; system-notifications -> allow T2 after 100ms latency budget breach
- Budget-based gating: tie a customer monthly token budget to maximum fraction that can use T0
- Telemetry surface: per-tier latencies, quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy or retrieval-based similarity), and cost delta
- Fast local simulator that replays a small prompt set and reports expected cost/latency under policies

Non-goals:
- Not shipping a full audit-compliant private policy manager yet
- Not building complex ML-based quality prediction in the prototype (heuristics only)

Proposed approach (stepwise):
1) Policy model: JSON blob attached to route config with priority list + triggers. Example: {"tiers":[{"id":"T0","models":["redwood-1"],"triggers":[]},{"id":"T1","models":["redwood-1-q8"],"triggers":[{"type":"latency","threshold_ms":300}]},{"id":"T2","actions":["trim_context","use_cache"],"triggers":[{"type":"budget_percentage","threshold":0.8}]}]}
2) Routing shim: small layer in hosted request pipeline that evaluates policy at request time and picks tier (fast eval, cached decision per session)
3) Simulator: CLI tool that sends a set of stored prompts through the routing shim under synthetic load/latency conditions and outputs a report (cost, tokens, quality proxies)
4) Rollout: feature flag + canary for 5% of routes, capture telemetry, allow quick revert

User stories (examples):
- As a growth PM, I want marketing bot to never use T2 so chat quality stays high for campaigns.
- As a platform engineer, I want non-critical summary jobs to automatically fall back to T1 during peak, so downstream latencies stay within SLO.
- As an operations engineer, I want to test a customer policy in the simulator before enabling it in prod.

Telemetry + metrics to capture:
- per-request picked_tier (T0/T1/T2)
- token_count and billed_tokens per tier
- end-to-end latency distribution per tier
- quality proxy: semantic-similarity-to-reference (embedding cosine) sampled per tier
- mismatch alarms: if quality proxy for T1 drops > X vs T0 for a route, surface regression

Experiment ideas (to validate):
- Small A/B: 10% of traffic for non-critical routes enable T1 on latency trigger=200ms. Measure cost delta and user-visible complaint rate.
- Synthetic burst: simulate 2x normal RPS and verify simulator predictions vs actual cost and latencies.
- Fallback sequencing: compare single-step downgrade (T0->T2) vs progressive (T0->T1->T2) for user satisfaction and total cost.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Need fast per-request eval, can't hit remote DB. Policy store must be cached in local node memory with TTL and watched for changes.
- Consider per-session stickiness window (e.g., once a session has T0 selected, keep it for N turns to avoid churn).
- Billing integration: must surface token accounting per-tier for clear invoicing.

Rollout plan (sketch):
- Week 0: spec + proto shim + simple JSON policy schema + unit tests
- Week 1: simulator + sample prompt sets (marketing, support, system messages) + small dogfood on internal routes
- Week 2: metrics dashboards + canary (5%) + incident playbook (how to revert if quality regressions)
- Week 3+: iterate on triggers (latency, queue-depth, budget), add session stickiness tunables

Open questions / risks (brain dump):
- How do we measure "quality" cheaply at scale? Embedding similarity sampling is expensive. Maybe sample 1% and extrapolate.
- Are there model architecture incompatibilities that make fallback outputs inconsistent (e.g., tokenization differences)? Need canonical normalizer.
- Legal/accounting: if policy causes cheaper tier use and customer disputes quality, what's the contractual surface? Add opt-in/opt-out flags for enterprise customers.
- Edge cases: tool-calling and function outputs when downgrading—should T1/T2 be allowed to call tools? Might need per-tier capability flags.

Quick notes to self:
- Build a tiny UI for policy JSON editing in Console later (raw to start).
- Add an "emergency force-T0" override for live debugging.
- Discuss with billing on how to emit per-tier line items for invoices.
- Put a short Confluence page summarizing the simulator methodology so SRE/QA can run reproducible tests.

Next actions:
- Draft an RFC for the policy schema (I'll start a PR in serving-runtime repo).
- Assemble 3 small prompt sets and save as fixtures for simulator (marketing-convos.json, sys-notifs.json, support-snippets.json).
- Slack poll with SE team: accept T1 for any route flagged non-critical? (ping Mika/Ava/Kai)

Random brainstorm snippets (freeform):
- Could use a tiny ML classifier to map intent -> tolerance (e.g., transactional vs exploratory) and then apply different tier thresholds. Keep for later.
- Idea: per-customer "quality budget" (e.g., can spend N high-quality responses / month) — gamify for freemium?

-- end of notes --
